title: How to Trade London Using TTrades Fractal Model
description: Learn how to trade London using the TTrades fractal model, daily bias, 4 hour candles, protected swings, and 15 minute confirmation.

body.text: Introduction
Trading London starts with the higher timeframe.

Before dropping down to the lower timeframes, establish a daily bias. Then let the daily wick form, use the 4 hour candle to find the swing you can trade away from, and finally use the 15 minute timeframe to confirm the protected swing.
The goal is simple: let the wick form, then trade the body.

This blog breaks down how to trade the London Session using the Fractal Model including daily bias, 4 hour wick, 15 minute confirmation, London reversals, and how the same fractal logic can be applied across different sessions.
Start With A Daily Bias
Before looking for a London entry, establish the daily bias.
There are different ways to do this using Phases of Price, daily closures, and EQ. The most straightforward approach is a Candle 2 or Candle 3 closure at a point of interest.
For example, price can expand into a fair value gap, close back through the series of candles that led into it, and form a new protected swing.
Once that closure confirms the reversal, we can anticipate the following candle to expand in that direction.
The point is to have a daily narrative before going into the lower timeframes.
Let The Daily Wick Form
Once the daily bias is established, do not immediately trade the daily candle.
The goal is to let the wick form and then trade the body.
If the daily bias is bullish, price can still trade lower before the expansion higher begins. If the bias is bearish, price can still trade higher before the expansion lower begins.
This is why the daily wick needs to form first.
A Candle 2 closure alongside the Phases of Price can give you the structure to anticipate the next candle expanding toward your draw on liquidity.
Use The 4 Hour Candle
Once the daily bias is established, move to the 4 hour timeframe.
Now the goal is to find a swing point to trade away from.
For a bullish setup, look for a low that forms before the expansion higher.
For a bearish setup, look for a high that forms before the expansion lower.
A Candle 2 closure can confirm the swing and give you anticipation for Candle 3 expansion.
But the same rule still applies.
Let the 4 hour wick form before trading the body.
This gives you the next layer of the fractal model.
Confirm The Swing On The 15 Minute
Once the 4 hour structure is in place, drop to the 15 minute timeframe.
The first thing to confirm is the swing point.
Look for a change in the state of delivery (CISD).
If price forms a low, find the series of candles that made that low and see whether price closes back through them. If it does, the reversal is confirmed and the low becomes a protected swing.
From there, look for the continuation that aligns with the daily and 4 hour direction.
This is where you can get on side.
The Full Fractal Model
The entire model can be viewed as the same process repeated across timeframes.
The daily candle gives you the bias. The 4 hour candle gives you the wick and the expansion structure. The 15 minute timeframe gives you the protected swing and entry.
Once those timeframes are aligned, you are simply looking for the lower timeframe confirmation to get on side with the higher timeframe expansion.
This is not a separate strategy for every timeframe. It is the same fractal model being applied across multiple timeframes.
London Session Timing
There can be useful Fractal Model setups during the London session, but the exact kill zone is not extremely important. The setup matters more than the specific time it forms.
The important thing is that the higher timeframe candle has formed its wick.
Depending on the market and the setup, the reversal can form in Asia or in the beginning parts of London. On the 4 hour profile, this can often be around the 2200 or 2am candle.
The clock itself is not what makes the setup valid.
The higher timeframe structure is.
London Reversals
There are also times when London forms the high or low of the day.
In that situation, look for a London reversal.
The idea is still the same. The 4 hour candle is forming its wick during London, and the 15 minute timeframe gives you the change in the state of delivery or continuation needed to get on side.
You are trading the London reversal while staying aligned with the daily bias.
A deep opposing run can make these setups more advanced. If there is SMT around the reversal, that can provide additional confirmation before looking for the lower timeframe continuation.
Failure Swings Need More Confirmation
Not every higher timeframe setup will give you a perfect swing.
Sometimes the Candle 2 closure creates a failure swing instead.
That does not automatically mean the setup cannot be traded, but more confirmation is needed.
If trading away from a failure swing, look for clean lower timeframe structure and continuation. SMT can also provide additional confirmation around the swing.
The farther price is from the failure swing, the more comfortable the setup can become. But the lower timeframe still needs to give you confirmation of the structure.
Holding The Expansion
When the higher timeframe candle is an expansion candle, there can be a lot of range available after the entry.
You can hold toward the highs or lows of the higher timeframe candle, depending on the direction of the trade.
You can also hold a runner toward the higher timeframe draw on liquidity.
This is where the model can produce strong risk to reward.
You are not chasing the initial move. You are getting on side after the wick has formed and then allowing the expansion to deliver.
How To Trade The Model
Keep the process mechanical.

Start by establishing the daily bias and letting the daily wick form. From there, move to the 4 hour timeframe and find the swing you are trading away from. Let that 4 hour wick form, then drop to the 15 minute timeframe and wait for the protected swing to confirm with a change in the state of delivery.
Once that confirmation is there, get on side with the continuation and trade toward the higher timeframe draw on liquidity.
Do not force the entry because London is open.
Wait for the structure.
Final Thoughts
The London session itself is not the setup.
The higher timeframe gives you the direction, the 4 hour candle gives you the wick and expansion structure, and the 15 minute timeframe gives you the confirmation to get on side.
Let the daily wick form.
Let the 4 hour wick form.
Then use the lower timeframe protected swing to trade the body.
You do not need to predict the exact high or low.
Let the market form the structure first, then trade the expansion.
That is the fractal model working exactly as it should.
